descriptionChirho: The abstract moral quality of conformity to God's standard of right — the dominant sense of צְדָקָה covering the vast majority of occurrences, rendered Arabic بِرّ (birr, piety/righteousness) or عَدْل (adl, justice), Korean 의/의로움 (ui/uiroum), Swahili haki/uadilifu; includes all singular inflections with article, construct, pronominal suffixes (my/your/his/our/their righteousness), prepositional prefixes (in/from/for/according-to righteousness), and conjunctions.

The plural צִדְקוֹת (tsidqot) denoting concrete righteous acts or deeds rather than the abstract quality — consistently rendered Korean 의로운 행위들 (uiroun haengwideul, righteous acts), Swahili matendo ya haki (deeds of righteousness), Arabic بِرَّات/صِدْقَات (birrat/sidqat, plural righteous deeds); includes plural construct forms with possessive suffixes and singular-tagged Kethib variants whose translations uniformly show plural meaning.

A legal right or legitimate claim — distinguished from moral righteousness by Arabic حَقّ (haqq, right/entitlement) rather than بِرّ, Korean 권리 (gweolli, right/entitlement) rather than 의로움, Hindi अधिकार (adhikar, right) rather than धार्मिकता, and Spanish derecho (right) rather than justicia; a rare but semantically distinct legal usage.
